content.title: Timberwolves vs. Celtics: Prediction, How to Watch for Free (3/22)
content.text: The Minnesota Timberwolves (43–28) face the Boston Celtics (47–23) tonight at TD Garden. Minnesota faces its toughest matchup entering its fourth game without Anthony Edwards, who’s been sidelined with knee inflammation. They’ve gone 2-1 without him, with wins against the formidable Phoenix Suns and the struggling Utah Jazz, followed by a 108-104 loss to the Portland Trail Blazers on Friday. The Timberwolves trailed most of the way against the Blazers, and by as much as 18, but climbed back late in the first half with an 11–2 run, powered by three shots from deep. The fourth quarter was a back-and-forth affair, with multiple lead changes. Donte DiVincenzo missed a layup with 11.3 seconds left that would have tied the game. Julius Randle led Minnesota with just 19 points on 6-of-16 shooting. Six Timberwolves players scored in double digits, but Edwards’ high-volume scoring and late-game clutch shooting were clearly missed. Minnesota sits in sixth place in the Western Conference, positioned for the final automatic playoff spot. They’re just a half-game behind the fourth-place Houston Rockets, with a four-game lead over the Phoenix Suns. There’s opportunity to secure a better seed — and a significant cushion to avoid falling into play-in tournament territory. The Celtics, meanwhile, enter on a four-game winning streak and four games behind the first-place Detroit Pistons. They edged out the shorthanded Memphis Grizzlies on Friday night, 117–112, powered by Jaylen Brown’s 30 points. Jayson Tatum struggled, making just 3-of-15 attempts from the field, finishing with 13 points. Luka Garza and Payton Pritchard combined for 41 points off the bench. With the Celtics entering at near full-strength, expect them to separate late and secure a comfortable win approaching double digits. Prediction: Boston Celtics 121, Minnesota Timberwolves 113 Injury Report Minnesota Timberwolves Anthony Edwards — Out (Knee) Naz Reid — GTD (Ankle) Boston Celtics Nikola Vučević — Out (Finger) How to Watch Timberwolves vs. Celtics Tip-off for tonight’s Timberwolves-Celtics game is set for 8:00 PM Eastern / 7:00 PM Central at the TD Garden in Boston.
